The setup converts every car of your Gran Turismo 1 and 2 discs into the packs (about 1700 cars).
The car catalog holds 2500 entries now.
Gran Turismo cars: GT1 engine sounds are taken from the disc into the car sound sets.
The car -> engine mapping is approximate (by redline). The RX-7 uses it.
Gran Turismo cars: car scale 0.135, ride height, and denting without the 255 vertex limit.
All real traffic now uses the full detail car model at any distance. The low detail model is only left for ambient cars.
The Car Detail Distance option is gone. The GPU cars make the full detail nearly free.

sections.title: CAR STREAMING
lines: Car streaming: the cars of the packs (Driver 1, Gran Turismo 1 / 2 ...) are a catalog. Cars of Driver 1 and the first cars of a pack are loaded at the start.
Car streaming: other cars load when traffic or the Start Car picker needs them, and are given up again (least recently used, never a car on the map).
Car streaming limits: up to 250 car models at a time (was 140), 1200 catalog entries (was 96), 1000 texture rows (was 250), 600000 car polygons (was 56000).
Fixed: car texture rows above 127 went negative (garbled cars when many cars were loaded).
New in a pack's cars\index.txt: kind=street|race|special (only street cars are traffic).
New in a pack's cars\index.txt: rarity=<weight> (default 10) and pin=1 (always loaded).
New developer variables: REDRIVER_STREAMCARS, REDRIVER_EAGERCARS, REDRIVER_STREAMCOPIES, REDRIVER_STREAMTEST.
The cars borrowed from the other Driver 2 cities stream as well.
Replays name the car of a player (not a slot), and the traffic pick no longer depends on what is loaded, so a replay shows the same cars.
The developer showroom loads every streamed car that fits.

sections.title: CITIES AND TRAVEL
lines: Driver 1 cities: Driver 1 cars in the traffic had oversized wheels hanging below the body, because the cosmetics file of a mod (BetterCars, for Rio) was laid over them. Fixed.
Driver 1 cities: mods no longer replace the cosmetics, denting and car models of a converted Driver 1 city.
Driver 1 cities: the Driver 2 cars of Rio (borrowed into the traffic) have their bodies and textures again.
Driver 1 cities: you get out of the car without a crash, and Tanner is in every city.

Driver 1 cities: the Driver 1 levels have no model of Tanner, so the converter adds his 16 body parts and his texture page to each city level. The setup does the same, taking RIO.LEV from your Driver 2 disc.
Take A Ride lists all eight cities in the new menu style: the four Driver 2 cities, plus San Francisco, Los Angeles, Miami and New York when installed.
Take A Ride: the city is always the day level. The time of day is the clock.
Take A Ride: Driver 2 cities offer Day / Dawn / Dusk / Night. Driver 1 cities offer Day / Dawn / Dusk. Los Angeles is a night city and always starts at night.
Per city data (map, labels, streets, gas stations, jobs, car sounds, level edits) is keyed by a city id now, so the Driver 1 cities no longer share Rio's files.
Driver 1 cities: planar water reflections from the water pieces of the edit pack (a flat piece with a texture named water...).
Driver 1 cities: the game makes a map picture from the level data for every city. It is generated on the first start and nothing is shipped.
Driver 1 cities: Los Angeles road spikes fixed (instance chains in the converter).
Level edits of the pack (the hand made water, canal and bridge pieces, also for Havana and Rio) ship in the Core pack.
Travel: Pause > Travel changes the city without restarting the game.
Driver 1 cities run a day-only clock (sunrise to sunset).
Gas stations in Havana, Las Vegas and Rio. Street lights in Rio and the Driver 1 cities.
Driver 1 cities: pedestrians walk the pavements. Run the setup again to convert the cities and get them.
Driver 1 cities: loading pictures with the city name.
Driver 1 cities: no more invisible cars (wheels only).
Driver 1 cities: Los Angeles lighting fixed.
Driver 1 cities: per city settings in cities\<NAME>.ini / config\city_<0-3>.ini (day only clock, brightness, paints).

sections.title: TRAFFIC
lines: The car you got out of is no longer removed by the traffic clean-up (the jam breaker and the density trim skip it). It stays at the gas pump while you fill up.
Only the normal distance rule removes the car you left, when you are far away.
Traffic cars: the Gran Turismo cars no longer appear in the traffic. For now they are for the customizer only.
Developer Options > Traffic Cars: Extended. On = the cars of the level, of the other cities of Driver 1 / Driver 2 and of the car packs you switch on. Off = vanilla, only the level's own cars.
Developer Options > Traffic Cars: one row per car pack.

sections.title: POLICE
lines: Police: the backup respawn time is the original 320 (it was 170).
Police: the cops' speed and strength follow the felony like the original game (no Survival strength at the top of the bar).
Police: the default Max Chasing Cars is 4.
Police Options > Patrol Cars (None / Few / Normal / Many, default Few): sets how many patrol cars the traffic carries.
Patrol Cars: the old value was Normal. With the busy traffic that meant about three cops around you all the time.
Police backup cars never appear in view. They are born out of sight (a 70 degree cone ahead up to 240 m, and 70 m all round).
Police backup cars are born at least 7 seconds of your speed away, and never closer than 100 m.
Police backup cars have no collisions until they are close and the way is clear, and they wait while their nose is in a wall.
The siren of your own car (the horn of a car with a siren) now flashes the cop lights on the street.

sections.title: GRAPHICS AND LIGHTS
lines: Options > Graphics: new Exhaust Pipes option (the 3D pipe models).
Options > Graphics: new Tail Lamp Glow option (the red lens of the tail lamps lights up).
Options > Graphics: new Handbrake Brake Light option, off by default. With it off, the handbrake no longer lights the brake lamps (this was one of the reports).
Options > Graphics: View Distance now goes down to 1 (the original game's draw distance).
The flat car shadow (Sun Shadows off) is the static original one again. It no longer stretches away from the sun into a big block.
Sun Shadows is the dynamic shadow system.
Reflections and the other graphics tweaks apply to the day versions of all four Driver 2 cities.
The water reflects the sky and clouds.
The black rectangle around a wheel whose hubcap came off is gone.
GPU cars: a chrome reflection (streaky sky / horizon sphere map, added over the body and glass) on every car: Driver 2, Driver 1 and Gran Turismo cars.
Chrome reflection strength follows the Car Reflection option and dims at night. Developer variables REDRIVER_CHROME / REDRIVER_GTREFL set the strength.
Cars: the chrome reflection replaces the old world reflection on the car bodies (one reflection, not two). It also works with the CPU car path.
Lights: L switches the headlights of your car on / off at any time of day.
Lights: K = high beams (longer, brighter beams).
Lights: J (held) puts the left pop-up headlight down (a wink).
Pop-up headlights (Gran Turismo 2 Nissan 180SX) move up and down with the lights.

sections.title: SOUND AND MUSIC
lines: Driver 1 sounds: crash sounds of Driver 1 cars are the real crash sounds of the disc (light thud, crunch, heavy crash). They used to be the steel barrier and wood fence clangs.
Driver 1 sounds: engine and idle loops play at the pitch of the disc (the per kind tuning is gone).
Run the setup again with the Driver 1 disc to get the new Driver 1 sounds.
Driver 1 cars: the light hit keeps the Driver 2 sound (the Driver 1 sample used for it was the steel barrier clang).
The setup makes 528 sound sets from your own Gran Turismo 1 / 2 discs, with every loop of the engine bank.
New layered engine sound type: carsounds/<set>.layers + <set>_L<k>.wav crossfade up to 9 loops over the rev range like the Gran Turismo games.
Gran Turismo 2 cars play the intake and the exhaust bank together. The gear shifts of Driver 2 are heard.
The sound state (music tracker, channel timers) is changed under one lock now (rare sound glitches).

sections.title: PERFORMANCE
lines: GPU cars: car bodies, undersides, wheel arcs, wheels, damaged cars, cars lit by dynamic lights, car shadows (shadow map), the far ambient traffic and the civilian pedestrians are drawn by the graphics card from static buffers.
GPU cars: before, this was done polygon by polygon on the CPU. The look is the same.
GPU cars: about 50 % more frames in dense traffic on a fast PC, and much more on an old CPU.
GPU cars: new option Options > Graphics > GPU Cars and config.ini [game] gpuCars=1 (0 = the original CPU path).
CPU use: the game used almost two CPU cores (180 - 190 % of one core, in the main menu too).
CPU use fix: the thread sleeps until the tick now and the limiter waits on a high resolution timer.
CPU use result: about 80 % of one core in play, 30 - 50 % in the menus, same 160 fps.
Logic tick cost: the traffic passes look at the cars of the grid cells around a car instead of all 160 slots.
Logic tick cost: the integer square root and the 128 bit division of the traffic maths use a floating point estimate made exact by integer checks (same numbers).
Logic tick cost: the sound emulation decodes a car sound once instead of at every start (starting a car sound took 1 - 5 ms inside the logic tick).
Logic tick of a rush hour with 116 cars: median 0.55 -> 0.42 ms, 99th percentile 2.0 -> 0.8 ms, slowest 6.4 -> 1.2 ms.
The traffic behaves exactly as before.

sections.title: MODS AND MENUS
lines: The button tooltips are translated.
The shipped config.ini has overrideContent=1 (the content override of mods with car models is on).
Fixed: BetterCars (and any mod with a DRIVER2 folder: car models, .cos cosmetics) did nothing.
Cause: config.ini shipped overrideContent=0, which switched the mod content off after the mods had asked for it. The mods now keep it on.

sections.title: SAFETY AND FIXES
lines: Replays: the ping packets stored the car slot in a signed byte, so with up to 160 cars the slots above 127 read as negative numbers. Fixed.
Replays now store a fingerprint of the simulation settings (traffic, AI, police, physics mode) and of the mods.
The log says when a replay is played with other settings ("it may play differently").
Boats: the cars that ride on a boat were a 32 bit mask, so with 160 cars every car above slot 31 stood still while the boat moved, and Tanner's bit landed on car 0. A real bit set is used now.
Level safety: the model tables have 2048 slots (a cell object type is 11 bits), so a damaged or modded level cannot read outside them.
Fixed: reading a damaged / modded level could index outside the model and texture tables (barrier scan, roof scan, far renderer).
Running out of memory now writes the size and place into logs\log.txt, shows a message and closes the game instead of crashing.

sections.title: LOGS AND BUILD
lines: Logs: the developer trace log logs/batchlog.txt (about 130 KB appended on every start) is only written when REDRIVER_BATCHLOG is set.
Logs: the bridge piece list logs/bridgelog.txt is only written when REDRIVER_BRIDGELOG is set.
Logs: shader / framebuffer failures and the bridge summary go into logs/log.txt.
A normal run now writes only log.txt, the engine log and a few small files.
The shipped exe ignores the developer / test environment variables (REDRIVER_*, 326 of them: test beds, traces, cheats of the dev tools).
Still working in the shipped exe: the Travel restart and the documented options REDRIVER_D1COP, D1FILES, D1PC, KEEPBARRIERS, RADIODIR, NOFASTCARS, NODEFERPRESENT, NOBATCHCACHE, BATCHLOG.
Batch cache: at most 2 files per level (was 4) and 1.5 GB for all levels together.
Batch cache: unfinished .tmp files of a crashed write are removed.

changelog.title: 0.3.0-beta   2026-10-12   (RELEASED publicly 2026-10-12 - everything since 0.2.0 is listed here; the 0.2.1 - 0.2.8 test builds were never published)

sections.title: CARS AND DRIVER 1 CONTENT
lines: Driver 1 cars from the PC release now have one 16 colour palette for every texture of the car (not one for the whole page).
Driver 1 PC cars keep their smooth shading and have six paints (the real palettes of the release).
Driver 1 PlayStation cars keep their original colours.
All Driver 1 cars use the Driver 1 engine and idle loops, with three Driver 1 horns pitched by kind of car (cop, family, luxury, old, muscle, sport, small, truck).
Added the Driver 1 crash sounds (light, medium, heavy) and the Driver 1 tyre skid.
The setup builds these sounds from the disc (Driver 1 Sounds mod).
Driver 1 cities (Pause > Travel) are marked experimental: the ground heights of the converted cities are not right yet and cars can fall off hills where the data jumps. That work is on hold.
The map screen and the minimap of the Driver 1 cities now look like the Chicago map (red streets, grey land, green parks, pale blue water; finer picture, 256 world units per pixel).
Mods can bring extra cars (mods/<name>/cars/index.txt + .d1c files, made from a car content mod).
Extra cars from mods appear in traffic in every city.
New config key startCar (file name of a car): Take a Ride starts in that car.
New in Options > Gameplay Settings: Start Car, Start Car Paint (six paints for cars that have them) and Restart With This Car.
Pick any mod or Driver 1 car and its paint, then restart to drive it.
Extra cities (experimental): the four Driver 1 cities (San Francisco, Los Angeles, Miami, New York 1978) can be converted to Driver 2 format by the setup from your own Driver 1 PC disc.
To add one, drop it into <game or mod folder>\cities\<NAME>.LEV (+ .img map, .ini name / start / gas stations).
Extra cities appear in Pause > Travel (Take a Ride) next to Chicago, Havana, Vegas and Rio. Choosing one restarts the game into that city.
They have the real streets, buildings, hills, civilian cars, traffic with lights, gas stations and a minimap. The night uses the mod's night lighting.
Not there yet in extra cities: pedestrians, lit night windows, roadblocks, special cars, a loading picture per city.

sections.title: POLICE
lines: Half of the police cars (patrols, chase cars and backup) are now Driver 1 cruisers with a light bar and the Driver 1 siren; REDRIVER_D1COP=<percent> changes the share.
Police need a clear line of sight now: a building between you and a patrol car hides you (no felony, no pull-over, a chase can be lost behind a corner).
Patrol cars are part of the ordinary traffic again, also while you are on a taxi fare or another job (they were never added during a job).
Police cars driving around or parked at the kerb with the civilian cars are real patrol cars: they watch for offences, pull you over and join a chase.
At most two driving patrol cars appear near you at a time; parked ones do not count.
Fixed: a freeze when the police backup was placed on a junction or off the roads (an endless search for a road piece at a fixed position).
Busted: it needs the police to see you, two or more cars closing in, you standing still AND the car unable to move more than 10 m forward or backward (a vehicle in the lane or a wall).
Standing still, watching something or hiding is no bust.
Busted ends the game, like drowning or wrecking the car in a pursuit; there is no fine any more.
In Take a Ride the on screen messages (offences, police) are at the top of the screen instead of the middle of the road view.
Police chases: backup cars are called in at the original rhythm (see below for where they appear).
The 'Dispatch: backup is on the way' call-out is gone, because it gave you too much warning.
Police (Take a Ride), part 2: backup is called during a chase. Extra cars appear far out of sight as ghosts, race to you and turn solid once they are close and nothing is in the way.
Backup spawn rate is about 10 % faster than the original.
The police get faster, stronger and ram you more the higher the felony; the top of the bar feels like Survival.
Boxed in by the police at a standstill = BUSTED (fine, the chase ends).
Offences within three seconds count once (the worst one), and a stop adds them all to one ticket.
The felony bar shows the worst of them and is cleared after the stop.
New Offence Severity list: how much each offence adds to the felony.
Traffic stops: you have 10 seconds to reach the stop point (60-100 m ahead).
Blowing past the stop point, driving off or ignoring the stop starts a chase at half the felony bar.
The officer walks to your door, faces it and talks to you: he asks if you know why he stopped you and lists the real reasons.
You answer with a popup: left = aggressive, right = polite, doing nothing = neutral (Y / N keys or the d-pad).
Every answer is a real line. The neutral one is said when you press nothing and just keeps the conversation going.
A polite answer sways the officer towards a warning or a dropped offence.
An aggressive answer is for fun (name calling, snappy comebacks) and costs you leniency; real abuse (calling him a pig) turns the stop into a chase.
Many more lines of officer dialog.
When the stop is over the officer walks back to his car and gets in, and the normal traffic AI takes the car again (new route from where it stands, lane change around you when there is a lane free).
Police (Take a Ride): up to 6 cars chase you (setting, 2..12). The vanilla Take a Ride sent only the patrol cars that happened to be near.
A chase needs more felony now (Chase Threshold: Classic / Relaxed / Lenient / Very Lenient, default Relaxed).
Light bumps, scaring pedestrians and property damage get a traffic stop on a clean record, like speeding does (Pull-Over Offences: Extended).
The felony cools down by itself once the cops lost you (Felony Cool Down).
New Police list in Options (main menu and pause menu).

sections.title: TAXI, JOBS AND RADIO TALK
lines: Taxi: fares pay more at rush hour (dusk, +30 %), at night (+15 %) and in the rain (+25 %), and the dispatcher says so in the offer.
Taxi: VIP fares (a singer, a quarterback, the mayor...) pay two and a half times the meter.
VIP fares have rules: no speeding and no bumps, three strikes and they walk, a flawless ride earns a bonus.
Night shift: tipsy passengers change their mind about where they are going and may grab the wheel; a patrol car that sees it pulls you over.
Night shift: dodgy passengers may run without paying; stop next to them within ten seconds and they pay.
Taxi: any cab that spawns in traffic (Driver 1 cabs too) can be used for fares.
Taxi: the drop-off marker shows the street name.
Serial stories: passengers sometimes tell a long story (about two to three minutes a part, with several choices) that lasts the whole fare.

There are five serials with three parts each: a bakery that is not just a bakery, the treasure of Uncle Mort, the night clerk of a haunted hotel, a wife with a secret life, the caller on the night radio.
If the fare or the part ends in the middle, the dispatcher can call you again with the same passenger, who picks up where he stopped ("Now, where was I?").
Serial progress is saved (saves\default\fare_serial.ini).
Only crashes cost mood now (red lights and the wrong side of the road do not).
An average above 60 mph for fifteen seconds without a crash is the fast bonus.
Taxi passengers are much more forgiving: speed, hard braking and police chases no longer upset them.
Only crashes cost mood, and a passenger only walks out after a lot of them.
Smooth driving and fast, clean driving earn a bonus on the tip (up to +40 %).
Passengers start talking 8-16 seconds into the ride (they hardly ever told a story before).
The talk panel of a passenger has a plain green light instead of the police lights.
Fixed: answering a prompt with the d-pad (CB offers, the taxi dispatcher, briefings, the officer, the passenger's questions) also changed the radio station.
The d-pad does not touch the radio while a prompt is open or for a moment after it closes.

More talk variety (GTA-style satire, PG-13): about 1,170 passenger stories and small talks now (revenge of the pigeons, the man who sold a 'genuine antique', a sandwich-shop heist, the mime in the box ...).
Four new CB themes: the absurd, fake commercials, crackpots, neighbours.
CB chatter comes about every 45 seconds.
Job offers come 1-2 minutes after a pass or timeout and 3 minutes after you accept one. Taxi dispatcher calls are unchanged.
People and talk: everybody you talk to in person has a name now (fares, and the traffic stop officer, e.g. 'Officer Kowalski').
Names come from about 330 male and 220 female first names and about 790 surnames. The dispatcher tells you the fare's name.
Passengers no longer comment on every bump. Their mood about your driving only moves the tip, and they remark on it now and then; they talk to you instead.
About 780 stories and small talks have answers: left = aggressive (rude, funny), right = polite, nothing = a neutral line.
Stories fork on what you say, every story has random names, places, food ... filled in, and the last 330 stories are not repeated.
The CB radio is ordinary 70s civilian chatter (not truckers): 360 situations in ten themes (traffic, weather, food, family, work, fun, gossip, radio talk, shopping, car trouble).
CB situations have comments, closing lines and openers that combine into thousands of different messages.
There are thousands of callsigns like 'Lucky Pike' or 'Stockyard Sam', and the last 90 situations are not repeated.
Taxi, part 2: pedestrians on the kerb wave down the empty cab; stop within 25 s (setting Taxi Hailing).

TOUR fares (about one in five in Chicago): the tourist names a district, you drive around in it for about a minute, he names the next; after three districts you take him back to his hotel, with a tour bonus on the fare.
The roof sign of the yellow cab is lit while it is free, and the cabs in traffic light up now and then.
Taxi: a dispatcher now calls the fares on the CB radio with street name, distance, direction, length of the ride and the estimated fare.
Dispatcher keys: Y takes the fare, N passes; the next call comes in 15-30 s.
Turn the dispatcher off in Pause > Gameplay > Taxi Dispatcher to get the old self-starting fares.
Passengers watch your driving: bumps, hard braking, speeding, red lights, the wrong side of the road and the police on your tail get remarks, their mood drops and so does the tip.
A passenger who has had enough gets out without paying. A long smooth stretch is praised.

sections.title: TRAFFIC AND PEDESTRIANS
lines: Pedestrians can be run over: they no longer always run clear of your car. Some are distracted, most are alert but a fast car leaves little time; honking and slow driving still make everybody dodge.
When the body of your car hits a pedestrian he is thrown, tumbles, bounces and slides along the road, then lies there with limp limbs for about 20 seconds.
Hitting a pedestrian is an offence (hit and run).
Switch: Gameplay > Run Over Pedestrians (also in the front end Police list). Traffic cars never hit pedestrians.
Traffic: fixed the heavy-traffic gridlock.
Cars in slots 128-159 (only used above about 125 cars) never moved because their id was a signed byte. Fixed.
Confused cars and parked cars that could not pull out no longer block lanes or pop out of existence.
Cars waiting for a gap to turn across traffic accept shorter gaps the longer they wait.
Measured in Chicago with 150 cars: cars moving without the jam breaker went from 32 % to 79 %, and jam breaker removals dropped from 626 to about 60 in 2 minutes.
Traffic signals rebuilt: every signalled junction now serves one approach at a time (straight, right and left of that approach go together, everybody else is red), in turn.
Signal cycle: 15 s green, then amber, then a short all red, then the next approach.
During amber nobody new may enter and the cars in the junction clear it (5 s, ini key lightAmberSecs). The all red time is set by lightClearSecs.
All junctions share one clock and the lamps on the heads follow it.
Opposite left turners and crossing traffic never move together any more (near collisions between crossing cars at signals went from 12 to 0 pair-seconds in my traffic test).
Turning cars no longer stop half way across the junction.
Right turners no longer wait for a car standing in the opposite lane of the road they turn into.
Parked cars beside the exit no longer block junctions.
Cars no longer change lanes within about 2 s of a junction (neither before nor after it). Turns are not affected.
Traffic and pedestrian density now follow the time of day (ini [game] timeTraffic=1, 0 = always full).
Density by time: rush hour 16:00-18:00 is 95-100 % of the configured limits, 8:00 about 80 %, noon 75 %, midnight 35 %, 4:00 about 25 %.
Extra cars are taken away one per second while nobody can see them. The limits come back as the clock moves on.
AI cars can drive to a destination (road aware, shared route data, no per-car planning; ambient traffic is untouched).
Auto-drive now drives to the waypoint you set on the map.

sections.title: CONTROLS, PADS AND WHEELS
lines: Controller: the extra buttons of a pad (back paddles / M buttons, e.g. of the 8BitDo Ultimate 2) can be assigned to any action in the controller rebind menu; press the button when the row asks for it ('Extra Button N').
Extra buttons only work when the pad reports them to Windows; try its D-input / Switch mode if the 2.4G / X-input mode hides them.
log.txt has a [pad] line with the number of buttons the pad reports.
Racing wheels (experimental): a steering wheel with pedals works as a controller; see Options > Controls > Wheel Controls.
Wheel Controls: Wheel Support (Auto / On / Off), and you pick the steering, throttle and brake axes by moving them.
Wheel Controls: invert switches, sliders for steering sensitivity / dead zone / curve / smoothing, and a dead zone + curve for each pedal.
Wheel Controls: a live view of the input, and Export / Import of the whole wheel setup as a .wheel file (config\wheel profiles) to share.
Wheel buttons are bound in Gamepad Controls like any other button.
The brake pedal also reverses. The wheel does not press menu buttons.
Wheel force feedback is off by default (Wheel Controls > Force Feedback (Experimental)).
Force feedback gives a centring spring that grows with speed and cornering, a pull when the car slides, a rumble for skids and road noise, and a kick in collisions.
Force feedback has sliders for overall strength, centring, road and skid effects and collision jolts, an Invert Force switch and a Test button.
Force feedback needs a wheel that supports it through DirectInput. It has not been tried on a real wheel.
Gamepad: new option Gamepad Control Mode (Analog Controls / Digital Controls) in the controller settings of the main menu and the pause menu.
The pad is held in the chosen mode all the time (the sticks could be dead after a load until Start + Select); Start + Select now flips the option.
Fixed: the Y / Triangle button of a gamepad did not resume the game from the first pause menu (only Continue did). The keyboard keeps its old behaviour.
Controllers and racing wheels keep working while the game window is not in focus (alt-tab, second monitor, recording software).
Gamepad: new option Swap D-Pad And Left Stick (Controls). The d-pad steers like the left stick (digital steering) and the left stick presses the d-pad directions (cruise, map, radio, menus).
With Swap D-Pad And Left Stick on, the HUD hints show the stick.
Fixed: the keyboard had no reverse with the Modern controls preset. The down arrow brakes and reverses now, also with the classic preset, like the brake button of the classic layout.
Gamepad controls have a Preset row at the top (main menu Options > Controls > Gamepad Controls and the pause menu).
Modern Controls preset: triggers for gas and brake, separate reverse, d-pad functions.
Classic Controls preset: the original PlayStation layout (X gas, square brake / reverse, circle wheelspin, triangle handbrake, the shoulders and triggers as before).
Rebinding a button afterwards shows the preset as Custom.
Fixed: a burnout (the wheelspin button) no longer stalls at about 50 mph. The hand-over to normal acceleration used to be treated as a light touch of the analog trigger (20 % power).
Controls can be rebound in both menus: Options > Controls > Keyboard Controls / Gamepad Controls.
To rebind, select a row and press the new key / button / trigger. Esc cancels, Del unbinds, Reset To Defaults restores all.
Bindings are kept in config\controls.ini on top of config.ini.
Controls: new Gamepad Steering Sensitivity slider (25-200 %).

sections.title: MENUS AND OPTIONS
lines: Menus (main and pause): Graphics is sorted into groups with headings (Quality, Lighting & Shadows, Reflections, World & Sky).
Menus: the HUD options and the day / night options moved to Display, together with Subtitles.
Menus: Police Options (Cop Difficulty is its first row) is in the Options list.
Menus: every option list has group headings (Display, Controls, Sound, Police Options, the keyboard / gamepad / wheel lists and the pause menu's Gameplay list).
Settings are saved as soon as you change them; you no longer need to quit the game.
Pause menu: new Exit To Windows entry (it saves and asks first).
Pause menu: Mods and Language are in the main pause list.
Pause menu: Options has Cheats and Developer Options (was Debug Options) at the end.

Developer Options only holds engine and test settings now (time and weather limits, rendering internals, traffic AI tuning, far density, economy and career numbers, debug overlays, skip mission, reset tweaks).
Everything a player would use is in the normal Options lists, only once (no duplicates).
The version text is in the title row of the pause menu.
Credits: Extras > Credits lists the project lead, the contributors (logos, BetterCars, Driver2TextureFixes, the 1977 Caprice) and special thanks.
Special thanks go to the original REDRIVER2 team, the input prompts pack and Reflections Interactive.
Credits also list translators, the libraries used and a short notice, and are translated into all languages.
Widescreen: the 4:3 pictures of the original menus, the loading screens and the movies are stretched across a widescreen window.
Options > Display > Menu Pictures chooses Stretched or Original 4:3 with black bars. The main menu picture and the game itself are not affected.
Main menu: new ultrawide main menu picture (3440 x 1440).
Pause menu > Options > Credits shows exactly the same credits as the main menu (scrollable).
The pause menu shows reDriver 2: Extended with the version and the build time.
First start: the graphics settings default to the Max preset instead of my test values.
Max preset: view distance 400; reflections on cars / wet roads / glass / water at 80 / 70 / 60 / 80; dynamic lights.
The main menu picture (mainmenu.png) of the core pack now ships.
Menus: "Mods (restart to apply)" became Mods with a small sublabel; the same for Conflicts (main menu and pause menu).
Fixed: Cop Difficulty and Subtitles were also written to tweaks.ini and could disagree with the profile. They are stored in the profile only now.
The pause menu can now be opened in the free camera too (not while the level editor is active).
Main menu: new Extras screen (Replays, HighScores, Secrets).
Secrets is one list: Mountain pass, Race track and Bonus gallery (the original secret screens, available without earning them).
Secrets also has toggles for invincibility, police immunity, player ghost, puppy dog cops, mini cars, Jericho mode and secret car.
Secrets has Unlock Everything (all missions, cutscenes, secrets and secret cars; saves the profile).
Options lost HighScores; Gameplay lost Controller and Vibration (Vibration moved to Controls, next to gamepad steering).
Main menu picture override: a PNG named mainmenu.png in a mod folder (or the game folder) replaces the main menu picture.
The picture can be any size and aspect ratio (for example 16:9 or 21:9 with a new logo). See tools\mainmenu\README.txt.
Options reorganized (main menu and pause menu): Display, Graphics, Controls, Sound, Gameplay, Language, Mods.
Display holds the graphics preset (Low / Medium / High / Max), window mode (windowed / borderless / exclusive full screen), resolution, FPS limit and VSync.
FPS limit choices: 25 / 30 / 50 / 60 / 100 / 120 / 144 / 165 / 240 or unlimited.
Display choices apply at once and are remembered in config\display.ini.
The preset changes view distance, reflections, shadows, grass, lights and so on in one step. It shows Custom when you changed a single value.
The main menu now has the same lists as the pause menu.
Sound: the main menu Options > Sound is now a list with SFX, music and radio volume (same list in the pause menu). The radio volume is remembered.
New sound mixer sliders, each 0-200 %: your engine, traffic engines, horns and sirens, tyres and skids, collisions, ambience and weather, voices, pedestrians and footsteps.

sections.title: HUD AND MAPS
lines: The tachometer lost the second dark plate behind the digital speed.
HUD messages (offences, police, mission messages) are drawn as a plate in the style of the top HUD panels, instead of yellow letters over the road view.
The message plate hangs under the objective / traffic stop panel when there is one, so it no longer overlaps it. The classic HUD keeps the old text.
HUD: the money is in a pill, moved clear of the fuel gauge.
HUD: the d-pad hints under the map show all four directions (Cruise = up, Map = down, Radio = left / right for previous / next station).
Left / right on the d-pad also answers a job offer, shown with the single left + right icon.
HUD: the damage and wanted bars are brighter and further from the map, so their icons no longer touch it.
HUD themes: Options > Display > HUD Theme switches between Modern 70s (walnut and orange), PlayStation (navy glass, steel bevels, Driver red and yellow) and Driver Menu.
Driver Menu theme looks like the main menu's option lists: flat translucent black panels, yellow headings, a dark red selection bar, no stripes, flat gauges and hint pills with a thin red rim.
Menu Style (Display) chooses how the pause menu looks, independent of the theme: as the theme says, a centred window, or a translucent side panel like the main menu's lists.
The Driver Menu theme uses the side panel.
Modders can add HUD themes as text files in <mod>\hud\themes\<name>.ini (name, ten colours, accent, corner roundness, bevel, menu, stripes, hud); see mods_README.txt.
HUD: the Driver Menu theme uses muted colours like the original release, more transparent panels and no bar on the hint pills.
Driver Menu theme: the red of the original minimap border is used for the rims and thin lines (map rim, tachometer rim, the line of the side panel menu).
The dark disc behind the tachometer is off by default; Options > Display > Gauge Background switches it on.
HUD: the three controls pills under the minimap are now a Controls hints panel (Cruise, Map, Radio, with the keys or the d-pad / stick icons).
The Controls hints panel pops up at the top right when a game starts and again every 10 - 15 minutes for ten seconds; Options > Display > Hints turns it off.
The minimap moved down to the height of the speedometer.
The whole minimap stack (map, bars, clock) is scaled down to the size of the speedometer stack; the map shows the same part of the city at a smaller scale.
The Driver Menu theme is the default for everybody (Options > Display > HUD Theme changes it).
The minimap has the same faint shadow as the gauges and is a little lighter.
HUD: the damage and wanted arcs fade out while there is no damage / no felony and fade in when it changes.
The keyboard icon theme defaults to Light.
HUD: the tachometer, the fuel arc and the MPH label have a faint drop shadow, so they stay readable on pale roads and sand now that the dark disc behind them is off.
New Hide HUD option (Options > Graphics, and the pause menu Graphics / Debug lists): turns off the gauges, map, radio panel and mission overlays for screenshots and videos.
Brand new in-game map: a pre-rendered whole-world map with road names that follow the roads, regions and gas stations.
The map has zoom and pan (keys and stick) and waypoints.
Rotating minimap with road names, pumps and a street name popup. The minimap zoom is an option.
New 70s styled HUD pieces: speedometer / tachometer, fuel, damage and wanted arcs that glow when they change, and a clock.
New input hints (CRUISE = the old Auto-Drive, MAP), job offer cards and pause menu panels.
Input icons: keyboard keys (square plates) or gamepad buttons (round pills), 5 icon themes, PS4 / PS5 / Standard / Xbox packs.
The pause menu panels show key / button hints underneath (up/down select, Enter / cross OK, Esc / triangle back).
Speech subtitles (cutscenes and mission speech) use the HUD font on a soft plate, larger and wrapped, and are correct for every language.
Hint pills fit their text in every language.
The minimap compass sits on the rim.
The map picture is dull like the original.

sections.title: WORLD, GRAPHICS AND LIGHTS
lines: Take a Ride: the barrier slabs that blocked Michigan Ave for no reason are taken out of the level; all other barriers stay.
REDRIVER_KEEPBARRIERS=1 keeps the Michigan Ave barriers.

Water reflections in every city: a flat edit piece with a custom texture whose file name starts with 'water' (like Chicago Water's water_blue.tga) gets the planar reflections of the city, at the height of that piece.

Water: the Chicago river, lake and sea are now an edit pack (mods/Chicago Water, 690 pieces) instead of being generated by the game, so they can be changed in the level editor. Keep that pack enabled.
Fixed: with the free camera far from the city (north edge, over open water) the screen stayed black for about a minute.
The cause was that the sky and the GPU scene were drawn into the minimap's small draw area.
Fixed: the level editor froze when hundreds of original faces were taken (faces are now matched through a spatial index).
Fixed: restarting Take a Ride at night (or any restart while it is night) put a map picture on the tree billboards.
The night texture swap had written a special model page over the minimap / tree page.
Tail lamps: the whole red lens of a car's tail lamp now lights up when braking, instead of a round blob in front of it.
Tail lamps also glow dimly when the lights are on.
Added Pause > Graphics > Light Cars and Light Lamps: how many cars and street lamps get real lights (up to 256 lights in all).
Every car on screen now gets both headlight beams.
Brake lights and headlight glows no longer sink into the bodywork.
Headlights are two proper beams at the real lamp positions (the player's reach further) and now light the road ahead.
Each tail lamp lights the street behind the car.
Car reflections are added on top of the car texture (strong at grazing angles and in the windows) instead of mixed into it, so the paint keeps its colour and detail even at 100 %.
The day / night texture swap now cross fades over a few seconds (both directions) instead of dipping to near black.
Fixed: after a restart at night the nearest buildings kept their night textures (dark walls, lit windows) once the day came.
The day / night swap now also covers the texture pages that a restart un-flags.
Fixed: beach / sand patches of grass tiles got grass blades. Blades now only grow on green textures.
The batch cache version was raised, so the first start rebuilds it.
Car reflections rebuilt: cars now reflect a live picture of the world around you (the real sky with clouds and sun, nearby buildings and road, day and night) instead of a painted skyline.
The new reflection has a soft Driver 1 style sheen and a sun glint.
The paint keeps its own colour: the reflection adds sheen and mirrors at the edges and in glass instead of tinting the car.
Car reflections cost about 0.05 ms of GPU time. Option: Options > Tweaks > Car Reflect (a saved 0 keeps it off).
Real water for Chicago's rivers and Lake Michigan (hand traced), at sea level. Turn it off with water=0 in config.ini.
Canal walls are filled under the bridges, and the water shows a planar reflection of the city.
Flat roofs on the open-topped building models and courtyard roofs in the city blocks (roofs=0 in config.ini turns them off).
3D grass on the grass tiles.
Sun and moon shadows (buildings, trees, cars, posts, bins, lamps).
Real sun and moon positions for Chicago, with moon phases.
Smooth day / night texture swap. Chicago day missions start at 4 PM.
Dynamic lights no longer bleed through walls, and translucent shadows are depth tested.
Free camera (F7) and high views draw the whole city. The horizon fog thins out with camera height.
Bridges, the ferris wheel, trains, ferries and helicopters are now drawn from far away (they vanished beyond about 15000 units).

sections.title: PERFORMANCE
lines: Performance: new Options > Graphics > Car Detail Distance. Cars farther than this use the low detail model, the biggest single saving in dense traffic; Max keeps 20000 units = 140 m of full detail cars.
Performance: the 3D grass is drawn per 60 m block and only where it can be seen (GPU time of the grass -60 %).
Performance: the whole frame copy into the PlayStation VRAM is skipped in the 3D game (about 0.25 ms per frame).
Performance: environment lookups of the options are cached (every car and many per-frame checks did a slow getenv).
Performance (second round): the cars are transformed once per vertex instead of once per triangle (the facing and depth tests are the same, checked on 11 million triangles).
Performance: the lit car path is only used when there is a light.
Performance: a finished frame is presented while the next one is being built (one frame more latency, no wait for the GPU).
In dense rush hour traffic at 1080p the game went from 176 to about 257 frames per second (99 % of the frames under the 165 fps budget).
REDRIVER_NOFASTCARS=1 and REDRIVER_NODEFERPRESENT=1 switch the two changes back.
Cars farther than carLodDistance (default 12000 units) use the low detail model: about 10 % more frames in dense traffic.
Trees, bushes and signs are drawn by the graphics card across the whole view distance (baked like the buildings and turned to face the camera by the shader).
They used to be drawn by the CPU only within 36 cells and popped out of existence beyond that.
The CPU saves about half a millisecond per frame, which helps older processors. Animated lights of distant objects keep animating.
The adaptive CPU draw ring now counts sprites as well as buildings when it decides how many cells the processor draws live.
Level loading is quicker: the baked level geometry is cached on disk (cache\batch_*.bin). The first start writes it, later starts read it.
The 0.7 s save wait at every start and the controller haptic probe are gone. Chicago loads about a second faster.
Adaptive CPU draw ring.
GPU batches for static buildings and ground tiles.
Region culling and render interpolation.

sections.title: PHOTO MODE AND REPLAYS
lines: PHOTO MODE (pause menu > Photo Mode): the game freezes, the HUD is hidden and a free camera starts at the game camera (WASD / mouse or sticks, Q E or triggers for down / up).
Photo Mode panel: camera speed, time of day, a colour filter (warm, cool, faded, sepia, night blue) and exposure.
Photo Mode panel: a vignette with its own strength, size, shape (oval / rounded / square) and colour (black / white / brown).
Photo Mode panel: cinematic bars (2.39:1, 2:1, 1.85:1), a thirds grid, a picture frame (white, black, instant photo) and a self timer (3 / 10 s).
Reset Effects clears the Photo Mode effects.
Photo Mode keys: Enter / A saves a JPEG of the picture without the panel to the Screenshots folder; H / B hides the panel; Esc / Y goes back to the pause menu.
FILM DIRECTOR / replays: the recording tape is about 228 times longer (684,988 instead of 3,000 pad records per player), i.e. hours instead of about 100 seconds.
The original code left only 13 KB of the 320 KB replay buffer for the tape; the buffer is 2 MB now.
A replay can have 250 camera cuts (was 60).
A replay can have 4096 auto director waypoints (was 150, about 8 minutes, after which the auto director stopped cutting).
Fixed: the auto director's waypoint pointer could run into the camera table; it is bounded now.
Replays saved with the new version are marked; replays of older versions still load (their camera table is 60 cuts).

sections.title: MISSIONS AND MISSION MAKER
lines: CUSTOM MISSIONS: Extras > Custom Missions lists the missions that mods bring (MISSIONS\M1000.D2MS to M1199) with title, city and mod.
Custom missions play with the Take A Ride rules; no career progress is touched, and the finish menu says Mission Complete / Failed.
The level editor (F6) has a MISSION tab to make custom missions without any file work.
Mission kinds: DRIVE (reach a goal), RACE (checkpoints in order against a time limit) and CHASE (wreck a target car that drives off when you come close).
Mission settings: time of day, weather, time limit, your car and paint, police, title and messages.
START and GOAL + are set at the camera crosshair; SAVE writes the mission into the edit pack and PLAY starts it right away.
MISSION MAKER, more kinds: TAIL (follow a traffic car to its destination without being seen or losing it).
MISSION MAKER: ESCAPE (the police come after you, lose them, reach the safe house).
MISSION MAKER: DELIVERY (pick up, deliver against the clock; the seconds left are paid as a bonus).
MISSION MAKER: CUSTOM (any steps in any order: go to, wreck, tail, escape, bonus).
The finish menu of a custom mission has a Custom Missions list to pick the next one, also in another city.
The mission text format names the texts inside targets too ("name" instead of byte offsets).
MISSION MAKER: REC CHASE / REC INTRO / REC OUTRO record a chase or the intro / outro cutscene of a custom mission straight from the game you are driving (no tool needed).
The mission script plays the recorded cutscenes by itself.
CUSTOM MISSIONS: texts follow the language (MISSIONS\M<n>.<Language>.txt of a mod, or the game's language files).
The mission maker's phrases are translated in all languages; a TRANSLATE button writes the files for translators.
New REC CHASE step: a car that drives a route you recorded (Take A Ride + Save replay + chase_tool).
Starting a custom mission from the editor or the finish menu reloads the level.
MISSION MAKER, script editing in the game: EDIT TEXT / APPLY / RESET TEXT.
EDIT TEXT shows every number, the script and the strings of a mission as text in your editor; it is built again with an error line on a mistake.
New console commands mission dump / build.
The mission panel shows the rows of the steps you use (marker size, target flees, tail range, escape time and wanted level, bonus base pay) and scrolls.
A tail step has its own distances.

sections.title: LEVEL EDITOR
lines: LEVEL EDITOR: sprites; FACE CAM turns the selected pieces to the camera.
Level editor: sample sprite objects tree_oak, tree_pine, bush_round, palm_tree in data\objects.
Level editor: small thumbnails in the object list.
Level editor: scrolling textures (SCROLL U / SCROLL V on the TEXTURE tab, speed = ANIM HZ).
Level editor: RAILS (kerb walls along the sides of selected DRIVE pieces, solid and slanted for ramps).
Level editor: a new piece without a picked texture takes the texture of the surface under the cursor instead of showing noise.

Level editor: barriers, street lamps, signs and other whole objects can be deleted now. Click the object to take it over; it is deleted as a whole and stays deleted, also when the area streams in again.
They used to be impossible to delete because the game draws them one by one and not from the batches the editor hides faces in.
Level editor: light markers now work live (no reload needed).
Level editor: new SLOPE collision shape cuts a solid into slices so it follows a slanted wall or slab.
Level editor: GLOW button lights pieces at full brightness (always or blinking), for signs and windows at night.
Level editor: animated textures (flip book). +FRAME adds the sampled texture as another frame, ANIM HZ sets the speed.
An in-game editor with a 70s panel and mouse control. It works on every level.
Edit, hide or replace original faces.
Add quads, boxes, polygons, prisms and OBJ imports.
Custom TGA textures (16 / 256 colours / direct colour).
Groups, arrays, undo / redo (400 steps), autosave, bookmarks and an in-game manual.
Pieces can be solid (traffic and pedestrians steer around them). Ground pieces are drivable (ramps, platforms).
Also: align / spread, a measure tool and a triangle budget meter.
Placeable copies of the level's own models (lamp posts, signs, barrels ...) and spinning pieces.
Gameplay markers: zones, checkpoint laps, spawn points, lights.
Edits are saved into edit packs (folders of mods\, default Level Edits).
In the editor you can switch, start, merge, archive or SHARE (zip) a pack. Each pack has its own object library.
Every enabled mod's edits are applied as locked layers, so edit packs stack and switch on / off in Options > Mods.

sections.title: MODS AND MOD MANAGER
lines: ONE CORE PACK: reDriver Core, Chicago Water, Vegas Water, Level Edits and the Driver 1 car sounds are now one pack, reDriver 2: Extended Core (folder mods\reDriver 2 Extended Core).
The Core pack holds the maps, icons, HUD, car sounds (the setup makes the Driver 1 engine files from your disc), the water / canal / bridge fixes and the level edits.
The level editor saves into the Core pack by default. An older ReDriver Core folder is renamed by the game.
MOD MANAGER in the main menu: Options > Mods switches mods on / off and moves them in the load order, with an info line per mod saying how many files it replaces.
MOD MANAGER: Show Conflicts lists the files that two mods both bring; the pause menu's mod list has Show Conflicts too.
Mods: the console command conflicts and the mod list's info line show which files two switched-on mods both bring.
Mods can now also bring tweaks (tweaks.ini), a HUD colour theme (hud\theme.ini), taxi passenger talk (fares\fares.txt) and package jobs (jobs\jobs.txt). See mods\README.txt.
Mod list in the options menu (Options > Mods): switch mods on / off and change their load order.
mod.json gives a mod a name, version, author, description and requirements. Order and switches are kept in config\mods.ini.
Old installs are migrated when you unpack this version over an old one.

sections.title: TOOLS FOR MODDERS AND CONSOLE
lines: Modder tools: pack_tool (new / check / pack / install / list mods) and chase_tool (recorded chases and cutscenes for missions).
Modding tools in the package as stand-alone .exe files: mission_tool, iso_tool, lev_dump, loc_report and the two Driver 1 car converters, with tools\MODDING_tools.txt.
Console (the key left of 1): new commands tweak [key [value]], hour, tp x z, missions, mission n.
Console: new command reload; mod tweaks, jobs, taxi talk and the language files are read again without restarting.
Modding: MODDING_GUIDE.txt (start here) and three sample mods in mods\_samples (tweaks, HUD theme, mission).
Modding: mission files (MISSIONS\M<n>.D2MS) can be written as text and built again (extract from the disc, dump, build, check).
A mod's mission replaces the game's mission of that number. The guide is tools\MODDING_missions.txt.
New debug tool: F4 shows a label over every standing traffic car with the rule that holds it, and a line to the car it waits for.
In F4 mode a timer shows top right. F10 saves a screenshot and the label log game\logs\trafficlabels.csv.
F4 no longer changes the keyboard controller.
The in-game console (the ` key) replaces the old console window: engine log and commands (help, lang, fps, pos, time, verbose, quit).

sections.title: SETUP AND PACKAGE
lines: Licenses: THIRD_PARTY.txt now carries the Independent JPEG Group acknowledgement, the rxi ini and stb_truetype notices and the right OpenAL Soft license wording.
The package has a licenses folder with the LGPL / zlib / IJG texts.
README, setup and tool texts say reDriver 2: Extended everywhere.
SETUP: more Driver 1 PC releases work: German, Spanish (re-release, its files are in the Joliet tree), French, Italian and English (Nero .nrg image) discs. All give the same 30 cars.
SETUP: disc images can be .cue / .bin / .iso / .img / .nrg / .pbp.
SETUP: long folder paths (over 260 characters) work, movies too (extended-length paths).
SETUP: long error messages under a disc row are no longer cut off (three-line area).
SETUP: the result list has no line limit.
The release ships The Long Way Home.txt and the mods BetterCars, Chicago Caprice and Driver2TextureFixes.
LINUX setup: reads Nero .nrg images and Joliet-only discs (Spanish Driver 1 PC re-release), like the Windows setup.
SETUP: the drive finder and the "game folder of another build" shortcut are gone from the setup window, because a drive scan is the kind of thing SmartScreen / antivirus programs dislike.
SETUP: the disc rows with Browse are all there is. The command line --import still works.
LOGO: the new reDriver 2: Extended logo is the icon of the game window / exe, the setup (window, title bar and installer header) and the modder tool exes.
SETUP LANGUAGES: the setup window and its messages are translated into the 12 languages of the game (Windows language, a language box on the first page, --lang xx). The log files stay English.
The movie converter (strconv.exe) takes UTF-8 names now, so a game folder with any letters (Greek, Cyrillic, Chinese ...) converts movies too.
SETUP: reDriver_Setup.exe is now a native Windows program written in C with a real setup window (no console window).
Setup pages: a welcome page, and a page for the disc images with one row per disc.
Disc page: every file is checked at once and named in plain words; wrong discs, Driver 1 discs in a Driver 2 row and plain .iso files are explained.
Disc page: a finder lists the drives of the PC and the disc images on them.
Setup pages: the destination folder (free space, earlier installation; nothing outside the game's own files is touched) and options with a summary.
Setup pages: a progress page (step and overall progress, moving bar when the time cannot be measured, log, Cancel that removes unfinished files).
Setup pages: a result page (what worked, skipped, failed; open the folder, start the game, view the log).
The installation runs in the background so the window never freezes.
The new setup makes the same files as the old setup did (disc images, cutscene audio, Driver 1 / PC cars, engine sounds, movies), checked byte for byte.
The only difference are the 16 colour palettes of the PC cars, which are now reduced by an own median cut with the same quality.
Setup command line options are unchanged (+ --dest); setup_log.txt and setup_report.txt are written as before. Linux keeps its own setup.
Linux: the package carries a linux folder (setup, movie converter built with cc) and redriver.sh (runs the game under Wine / Proton).
The Linux files are not tested on a real Linux system yet; see linux/README_LINUX.txt.
Setup: writes setup_report.txt every run (system details, results, full log).
Setup: a disc it does not know or cannot use is analysed ONLY after asking (names, sizes, ids; no game data) into setup_disc_report.txt.
Linux tools write install_log.txt / launch_log.txt; linux/collect_report.sh packs them.
The old DRIVER2 / d1cars / install / maps / icons / carsounds folders are moved into GAME_DATA and mods\ReDriver Core. Nothing is overwritten or deleted.
The disc image path in config.ini follows the move.
The setup converts the PlayStation movies itself (no Java). It takes about a minute and needs 0.7 GB instead of 1.3 GB.
New folder layout: GAME_DATA, config\ (settings), logs\ (all logs), cache\ (generated files, safe to delete), mods\ReDriver Core, and radio stations inside the game folder.
Settings from older versions are migrated.
The exe is named reDriver2_extended.exe, the window title is "reDriver 2: Extended", and the game has an application icon.
The shipped exe is stripped (3 MB).

sections.title: LANGUAGES AND FONTS
lines: The new texts (taxi, police, options) are translated into all 12 languages (machine translations, native speaker review welcome).

Fonts: the HUD and the added letters of the game fonts (Greek, Cyrillic, Latin Extended) now use open fonts (Jost, Caprasimo, Archivo Black, Anton, Noto Sans; SIL Open Font License) instead of Microsoft fonts.
The look is close to the old one (geometric sans, a Cooper Black style soft serif for titles).
Fixed: the front end font had no @ # + = < > ~ ^ | \ ' " (they were blank, e.g. in the credits e-mail address). They are drawn now.
Language option (pause > Options, Language): French, German, Italian, Spanish, Czech, Slovak, Polish, Hungarian, Russian, Greek, Turkish and Romanian (plus English).
Everything the mod added is translatable: menus, HUD, jobs, CB radio, police stops, money and fuel texts, speech subtitles and credits headings.
Translation files are plain text in localizations\<language>\. See localizations\README.txt to add or improve a language.
Texts are UTF-8 now.
The HQ fonts and the HUD cover Latin (with Central European letters), Romanian comma letters, Greek and Cyrillic. Movie subtitles use the same fonts.
The remaining ~476 speech subtitle lines of French, German, Italian, Spanish, Czech, Slovak, Polish and Hungarian are machine translated now.
The cutscene lines are short sentence fragments, so some will read oddly. Corrections from native speakers are welcome.
Translations can be checked with the loc tool (see localizations\README.txt).
FontTool (game\tools\FontTool) builds the HQ fonts for more languages.

sections.title: SAVES AND GAMEPLAY
lines: Saved games are plain text files in the game's saves\default folder instead of binary files hidden in your user folder.
profile.sav holds settings, furthest mission, secrets and high scores; progress.sav holds the continue point; money.ini, respect.ini and fare_serial.ini hold the career.
Copy or zip the saves folder to back it up or share it. REDRIVER_PROFILE=<name> keeps another player's saves in saves\<name>.
Every save file has a format number, unknown entries are ignored and written back, and missing ones get defaults.
The previous version of each save file is kept as .bak, so an update will not break your saves. Old saves are picked up automatically.

All four cities (Chicago, Havana, Las Vegas, Rio) are selectable in Take a Ride and the other free modes from the start (ini [game] unlockCities=1; 0 = only after the story missions like the original).
New Physics Speed option (pause > Options > Gameplay): NTSC (30 Hz, default) or PAL (25 Hz, slower).
Mission timers keep counting real seconds in both modes.

sections.title: FIXES
lines: Fixed: a crash caused by the street lamp damage counter running one past its table (found from a crash log).
Physics Speed (PAL): job and CB timers, police stop timers, fuel use, the pump rate, the day clock and the speedometer follow the real tick rate, so a second stays a second in both modes.
The in-game console no longer lists harmless messages (no haptics, waiting for the disc read).
Mission cinematics: ground, walls and cutscene cars vanished in parts (old depth / stencil data of the previous frame survived). Fixed.
The ferris wheel and other animated events disappeared at distance. Fixed.
Cutscene subtitles and the credits use the HQ font for all letters.
No more '?' for accented or Cyrillic letters in menus.
Fixed "CdSearchFile called while in CdlReadS" console spam.
Fixed missing-glyph warnings.
Fixed lifting bridges at distance.
Fixed night textures after a restart.
Fixed tree texture squares at night.
Fixed far building fronts missing.
Fixed shadows visible through buildings.
Fixed a rare crash (division by zero in the angle code) when far-away objects were drawn.

changelog.title: 0.2.0-beta   (first complete public beta package)
intro: Everything from the 0.1.x test builds below, in one package, plus a polished setup and docs.

sections.title: NEW AND IMPROVED SINCE 0.1
lines: Setup (reDriver_Setup.exe) is now a guided console setup that explains each step and gives hints.
Setup asks for BOTH Driver 2 discs up front.
Setup recognizes the disc release (USA, Europe, France, Germany, Italy, Spain) and sets the game language to match.
Setup offers a retry when the wrong disc is picked.
Setup shows progress and ends with a summary.
Setup writes setup_log.txt, which you can attach to bug reports.
Cutscene and mission audio (voices and music) is now decoded from your disc by the setup. Cutscenes were silent before.
Optional movie conversion (needs Java), including the disc 2 movies for Vegas and Rio.
Setup can reuse the cutscene audio and movies that another REDRIVER2 build already extracted (--import).
Driver 1 (PlayStation) cars are converted from your discs.
The 30 PC-only cars from the Driver 1 PC disc (Ferrari 250 SWB, Thunderbird ...) are converted from your discs too.
Driver 1 cars use the Driver 1 engine sound.
16 engine sound types are shipped in the carsounds folder.
You can add any number of your own sound sets and assign them in carsounds\sounds.txt.
Driver 2 cars keep their original sounds unless you change that.
New mods folder: drop REDRIVER2 content mods (texture packs, car packs) into mods\. Nothing is overwritten. See mods\README.txt.
Mods follow the day / night cycle and the whole-map textures.
Added keyboard keys for everything that was gamepad-only: T auto-drive, M map, Y / N for CB jobs, and , and . for the radio.
LB / RB change the radio station on pads without a D-pad.
On-screen hints show keyboard keys or gamepad buttons, depending on what you use.
Pause menu > Options > Controller Settings now lists all controls.
Keyboard walking works while a controller is connected (Steam Input etc.).
The version number is shown in the pause menu.
The X/Y/Z position display is now off by default.
The game writes log.txt (the previous run is kept as log_prev.txt) with system, graphics, performance and crash information.
F10 marks a problem in the log and takes a screenshot.
collect_report.bat packs everything needed for a bug report.
Windows 7 / 8 and 32-bit Windows are supported: the game and setup are 32-bit, and the Universal C Runtime installer is included.

sections.title: FIXED
lines: Fixed whole-screen flicker on some frames (water-only frame). The frame is now presented in one piece.
Silent cutscene cars no longer have working headlights or exhaust smoke.
CB job popups now only appear in free roam.
Texture mods were overwritten by the day / night swap. This is fixed.
Texture mods were ignored on the distant city pages. This is fixed.
Fixed garbage textures on some Driver 1 / PC cars.
Fixed the wheel positions of tall vans.
Known issues: see README.txt.
0.1.24 - 0.1.15   (test builds)
0.1.24: keyboard walking while a controller is connected.
0.1.23: mods folder; texture mods follow day / night and the whole-map textures.
0.1.22: controls lists in the pause menu.
0.1.21: keyboard auto-drive, map and CB job answers; hints that match your input device.
0.1.20: radio station keys (keyboard , and . and LB / RB).
0.1.19: setup can reuse data from another REDRIVER2 build.
0.1.16: setup requires both Driver 2 discs up front.
0.1.15: friendlier setup.
0.1.14: setup reads the Driver 1 PC disc (InstallShield reader built in).
0.1.13: car sound sets are shipped.
0.1.12: bigger sound memory.
0.1.11, 0.1.10, 0.1.9: car sound system and the Driver 1 engine sound.
0.1.8: version shown in the pause menu.
0.1.8: other disc regions (serial detection, language, Driver 1 tables, level lookup by directory).
0.1.7: optional movie conversion.
0.1.6: cutscene audio.
0.1.5: F10 marks and collect_report.bat.
0.1.4: log.txt.
Flicker fix.
32-bit game and setup exe.
Universal C Runtime.
First beta packaging (0.1).
